newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Commodity Exchange says may list crude oil.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Commodity Exchange says may list crude oil.

text.p: The Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) said on Friday that proposed deregulation of foreign exchange markets would make it easer to list dollar-denominated crude oil futures.
"Listing crude oil futures has become increasingly viable because of plans to ease restrictions on Japan's foreign exchange market," said Mitsuhiro Onosato, TOCOM's planning department manager.
"A crude futures contract in Tokyo would also help answer the growing demand for a new benchmark crude in Asia," he said.

Crude oil is traded in dollars throughout the world, meaning a crude futures contract would be ideally denominated in dollars to avoid risks from fluctuations in the foreign exchange market, industry sources say.
Last December an advisory panel to the finance minister announced a sweeping plan to deregulate Japan's foreign exchange market in 1998, in a bid to enhance international competitiveness.
The plans include easing restrictions on dollar-denominated transactions, making dollar-denominated commodity futures contracts more accessible to investors, Onosato said.
TOCOM already has plans to list yen-based gasoline futures from fiscal 1998/1999 starting April 1, and is studying the potential of listing gas oil and kerosene futures, both based in yen.

Oil traders in Asia have called for the need to create a new benchmark crude, in light of the declining role of Tapis crude as a benchmark for regional grades and Dubai crude for Middle Eastern crudes.
Onosato said a crude contract on TOCOM would help solve the problem.
"A dollar-denominated contract would be attractive to foreign investors and if listed in Tokyo, chances of liquidity being high are great," he said.
On types of crude, Onosato said Brent blend crude, which is also listed on the Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX), as well as in London, was the strongest candidate.
"The liquidity of Brent futures on SIMEX is thin, however, in Japan we can expect a substantial amount of funds flowing into the market," Onosato said.
Gold, silver, platinum, palladium, rubber, cotton and wool futures contracts are traded on TOCOM. The exchange will list an aluminium futures contract from April.
